This is a high-priority clinical treatment-context gap, not evidence for or against muscle rescue.

records.title: Mad2 and BubR1: chemotherapeutic coordinators in gastric cancer.
records.interpretation: Full commentary summarizes Mad2/BubR1 knockdown in gastric cancer: lower proliferation/migration/invasion and reduced paclitaxel sensitivity, with senescence-like responses implicated rather than altered apoptosis. Cisplatin and bleomycin sensitivity did not change in the cited primary study. This concerns cancer chemotherapy response, not healthy-tissue rescue; primary experiment is PMID25483095.
records.model: Gastric cancer cells with Mad2 or BubR1 depletion, summarized from Bargiela-Iparraguirre et al.
records.endpoint: Growth, migration/invasion, chemotherapy sensitivity, senescence-associated beta-galactosidase, p53 and IL6/IL8
records.access_limitation: Complete indexed official PMC body and references read; direct PMC browser check and publisher PDF403. Additional chemotherapy drugs mentioned only as clinical background were not counted as administered experiments.

records.title: Sirtuin to the rescue: SIRT2 extends life span of BubR1 mice.
records.interpretation: Full commentary attributes lifespan/cardiac improvement in BubR1 hypomorph mice to genetic SIRT2 overexpression, while small size, cataracts and lordokyphosis persist. It explains K668 deacetylation-mediated BubR1 stabilization and proposes NAD precursors NMN/NR as a future therapeutic route; it is not an independent drug lifespan/rescue experiment. Primary North et al. 2014 study remains the experimental source.
records.model: Genetic SIRT2-transgenic cross with BubR1-H/H mice and mechanistic biochemical work summarized from North et al.
records.endpoint: Median/maximal lifespan, cardiac function, BubR1 protein stability, persistent tissue-specific progeroid phenotypes
records.access_limitation: Complete indexed official PMC commentary body and references read after direct page browser check. Figure image not independently interpreted; no new validation of cited primary experiments. Failed BioC payload was documentation/error, not recovered article text.

records.title: BubR1 highlights essential function of Cdh1 in mammalian oocytes.
records.interpretation: Complete commentary explains BubR1/Cdh1 control of oocyte prophase arrest and meiotic progression. It proposes different knockdown extent as one explanation for opposing Wei versus Homer meiotic phenotypes, explicitly calling the reconciliation suppositional. This is mechanistic interpretation of genetic perturbations, not a new drug rescue or independent experimental confirmation.
records.model: Antisense BubR1/Cdh1 depletion in mammalian oocytes, discussed from Wei and Homer primary studies
records.endpoint: Cdh1 stability, APC activity, cyclin B1/securin/Cdc20 balance, prophase arrest and meiosis I completion
records.access_limitation: Complete target commentary read across indexed official PDF pages1029–1030, including figure legend, ending and nine references. PDF is a News & Views bundle; unrelated Chk1/p53 drug passages were excluded. Direct PDF download403.

records.title: ANTIBODY SPECIFIC FOR BUBR1
records.interpretation: Complete patent abstract and all 16 claims were read, plus an incomplete description. Claims concern antibodies recognizing acetylated BubR1 (human K250 and species equivalents), assay kits and sample-based detection, including cancer specimens. They do not claim administering the antibody as an MVA treatment. This is an analytical reagent disclosure, not an independent therapeutic rescue experiment.
records.model: Antibody recognition of acetylated BubR1 in samples; species variants and acetylation-mimicking substitutions in claims
records.endpoint: Selective acetylation detection and diagnostic/research kit use
records.access_limitation: Original Korean and machine-translated English abstract and claims accessible; only part of the lengthy description was read. Supplemental depth is complete abstract, not complete patent body. Translation limits apply.

records.title: BubR1, a spindle assembly checkpoint protein in mammalian oocyte meiosis.
records.interpretation: Complete page 1458 commentary on Wei et al. explains that BubR1 depletion disrupts mouse-oocyte checkpoint arrest and chromosome alignment, including failure of low-dose nocodazole to maintain arrest. It also contrasts Homer et al.'s prophase/prometaphase result. Nocodazole is a damaging checkpoint probe, not rescue therapy. The commentary adds no independent experimental cohort.
administered_agents: nocodazole (checkpoint-disruption assay in cited primary work)
records.model: Mouse oocytes with altered BubR1 expression, summarized from Wei et al. PMID20237433 and Homer et al.
records.endpoint: Germinal-vesicle breakdown, chromosome alignment, kinetochore-microtubule attachment and nocodazole-induced meiotic arrest
records.access_limitation: Complete target commentary, ending and references recovered from indexed official publisher PDF. PDF bundles several News & Views articles; other articles on the same file/pages were not attributed to this title. Direct PDF download returned403.

limits: Historical saved-corpus depth and empty/absent abstract hashes are preserved; supplemental depth does not rewrite them.

Complete body means the entire target textual article/commentary/correction was read, including its ending and references where present; original experimental figures were not independently revalidated.
Nine complete bodies are six commentaries/highlights and three corrections, not nine independent treatment studies.
The patent abstract and all16 claims were read, but only part of its description.
Two partial and seven title-only records cannot support absence-of-intervention conclusions.
Indexed official publisher/PMC pages were used where direct requests produced browser checks or403; no access controls were bypassed, no accounts created and no authors contacted.
interpretation: Every historical title-only record received an access/recovery assessment, not a complete-content review. Supplemental text/abstract reading is separate from the fixed original corpus. Commentaries/corrections do not add independent experiments. No raw abstracts or manuscript text are included.
